Questions 27 and 28

Choose the correct letter，A，B or C.

27 What do the speakers say about the evidence relating to birth order and academic success?

Choose TWO letters，A-E.

Which TWO experiences of sibling rivalry do the speakers agree has been valuable for them？

transcript.en: Ed, how are you getting on with the reading for our presentation next week?
transcript.zh: 埃德，我们下周的报告阅读情况怎么样了?

transcript.en: Well Okay, Ruth. But there’s so much of it.
transcript.zh: 好吧,露丝。但还有很多。

transcript.en: I know. I hadn’t realized birth order was such a popular area of research.
transcript.zh: 我知道。还没有意识到出生顺序是一个如此受欢迎的研究领域。

transcript.en: But the stuff on birth order and personality is mostly unreliable. From what I’ve been reading, a lot of the claims about how your position in the family determines certain personality traits are just stereotypes with no robust evidence to support them.
transcript.zh: 但是关于出生顺序和性格的资料大多不可靠。从我所读到的来看，很多关于你在家庭中的地位如何决定某些性格特征的说法都是刻板印象，没有有力的证据来支持它们。

transcript.en: Okay, but that’s an interesting point. We could start by outlining what previous research has shown. There are studies going back over a hundred years.
transcript.zh: 好，这是个有趣的观点。我们可以先概述一下之前的研究成果。有些研究可以追溯到一百多年前。

transcript.en: Yeah. So we could just run through some of the typical traits, like the consensus seems to be that the oldest children are generally less well-adjusted because they never get over the arrival of a younger sibling.
transcript.zh: 是的。所以我们可以简单回顾一下一些典型的特征，比如大家一致认为最大的孩子通常适应能力较差，因为他们从来不能从弟弟妹妹的到来中缓过来。

transcript.en: Right, but on a positive note, some studies claimed that they were thought to be good at nurturing, certainly in the past when people have large families. They would have been expected to look after the younger ones.
transcript.zh: 对，不过从积极的方面来说，一些研究称他们擅长养育孩子，尤其是在过去有大家庭的时候。他们会被期望去照顾这些年轻的孩子。

transcript.en: There isn’t such a clear picture from middle children. But one trait that a lot of these studies mention is that they are easier to get on with their older or younger siblings.
transcript.zh: 中间的孩子没有这么清晰的形象。但这些研究提到的一个特点是，他们更容易与年长或年幼的兄弟姐妹相处。

transcript.en: Generally eager to please and helpful --although that's certainly not accurate as far as my family goes--my middle brother was a nightmare-- always causing fights and envious of whatever I had.
transcript.zh: 一般来说，(中间的孩子)都渴望取悦和帮助他人。但这种说法不适用于我的家庭。我的二哥是个噩梦，总是引起争斗，嫉妒我所拥有的一切。

transcript.en: As I said, none of these seem to relate to my own experience. I’m the youngest in my family and I don’t recognize myself in any of the studies I’ve read about. I’m supposed to have been a sociable and confident child who made friends easily, but I was, actually, terribly shy.
transcript.zh: 就像我说的，这些似乎都与我自己的经历无关。我是家里最小的孩子，在我所有读到的研究中，我不属于任何一类。我应该是一个善于交际、自信的孩子，很容易交到朋友，但实际上，我非常害羞。

transcript.en: Really? That’s funny. There have been hundreds of studies on twins, but mostly about nurture vs nature.
transcript.zh: 真的吗?这真有趣。已有数百项关于双胞胎的研究，但大多是关于后天培养与先天天性的。

transcript.en: There was one on personality, which said that a twin is likely to be quite shy in social situations because they always have their twin around to depend on for support.
transcript.zh: 有一个研究是关于个性的，它说双胞胎中的一个在社交场合可能会害羞，因为他们总是有他们的双胞胎兄弟可以依靠。

transcript.en: My cousins were like that. When they were small, they were only interested in each other and found it hard to engage with other kids. They are fine now, though.
transcript.zh: 我的堂兄弟们就是这样。当他们小的时候，他们只对彼此感兴趣，很难和其他孩子交流。尽管后来他们意识到了。

transcript.en: Only children have had a really bad press. A lot of studies have branded them as loners who think the world revolves around them because they've never had to fight for their parents’ attention.
transcript.zh: 独生子女受到了很重的舆论压力。许多研究把他们打上“孤独者”的烙印，认为世界围绕着他们转，因为他们从来不必去争取父母的关注。

transcript.en: That does seem a bit harsh. One category I haven’t considered before was children with much older siblings. A couple of studies mention that these children grow up more quickly and they are expected to do basic things for themselves like getting dressed.
transcript.zh: 这听起来确实有点刺耳。我以前从未考虑过的一类是有大得多的兄弟姐妹的孩子。几项研究提到，这些孩子成长得更快，他们被要求为自己做一些基本的事情，比如穿衣服。

transcript.en: I can see how that might be true, although I expect that sometimes the exact opposite, playing the baby role, and clamouring for special treatment.
transcript.zh: 我知道这可能是真的，尽管我认为有时恰恰相反，他们会扮演婴儿的角色，大声要求特殊待遇。

transcript.en: What was the problem with most of these studies, do you think?
transcript.zh: 你认为这些研究有什么问题吗?

transcript.en: I think it was because in a lot of cases, data was collected from only one sibling per family who rated him or herself and his or her siblings at the same time.
transcript.zh: 我认为这是因为在很多情况下，每个被调查的家庭只有一个兄弟姐妹，所以他们同时给自己和兄弟姐妹打分。

transcript.en: Umm...Some of the old research into the relationship between the birth order and academic achievement has been proved to be accurate though. Performances in intelligence tests decline slightly from the eldest child to his or her younger siblings. This has been proved in lots of recent studies.
transcript.zh: 嗯……一些过去的关于出生顺序和学术成就之间关系的研究已经被证明是正确的。从老大到弟弟妹妹，智力测试的表现略有下降。这在最近的许多研究中得到了证实。

transcript.en: Yes, although what many of them didn’t take into consideration was family size. The more siblings there are, the likelier the family is to have a low socio-economic status, which can also account for differences between siblings in academic performance.
transcript.zh: 是的，虽然他们中的许多人没有考虑到家庭规模。兄弟姐妹越多，家庭的社会经济地位越低，这也可以解释兄弟姐妹之间学习成绩的差异。

transcript.en: The oldest boy might be given more opportunities than his younger sisters, for example.
transcript.zh: 比如说，最大的男孩可能会比他的妹妹有更多的机会。

transcript.en: Exactly.
transcript.zh: 没错。

transcript.en: But the main reason for the marginally higher academic performance of oldest children is quite surprising, I think. It’s not only that they benefit intellectually from extra attention at a young age, which was what I would have expected. It’s that they benefit from being teachers for their younger siblings by verbalizing processes.
transcript.zh: 不过我认为最年长的孩子学习成绩稍微好一点的主要原因是非常令人惊讶的。他们不仅在智力上受益于小时候的额外关注，这也是我所想到的。而且他们受益于做他们的弟弟妹妹学习语言表达过程中的老师。

transcript.en: Right, and this gives them status and confidence, which again contributes in a small way to better performance.
transcript.zh: 是的，这给了他们地位和信心，这也有助于他们取得更好的成绩。

transcript.en: So would you say sibling rivalry has been a useful thing for you?
transcript.zh: 你会说兄弟姐妹之间的竞争对你很有帮助吗?

transcript.en: I think so. My younger brother was incredibly annoying, and we fought a lot. But I think this has made me a stronger person. I know how to defend myself. We have some terrible arguments. And I would have died rather than apologize to him. But we had to put up with each other and most of the time we coexisted amicably enough.
transcript.zh: 我想是的。我的弟弟非常烦人，我们经常吵架。但我认为这让我成为了一个更坚强的人。我知道如何保护自己。我们有一些过激的争论。我宁愿死也不愿向他道歉。但我们必须互相容忍，大多数时间我们都相处得很融洽。

transcript.en: Yes. My situation was pretty similar. But I don’t think having two older brothers made me any less selfish. I was never prepared to let my brothers use any of my stuff. That’s perfectly normal. Well, sometimes......
transcript.zh: 是的。我的情况也差不多。但我不认为有两个哥哥会让我变得不那么自私。我从不能让我的兄弟用我的东西。这是完全正常的。嗯,有时候……
